“One of the central premises of our republic is that power without checks and balances will be abused.” @SolveigSinglet argues CFPB subpoenas are too often broad, vague, and costly—Congress should curb this “superpower.”

ow.ly/hxhQ50Z2m5b

Energy is massively abundant — and always will be, says Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright.
 
Watch his full remarks at the Cato Institute on the current state of energy policy — and the revolutions to come: ow.ly/5zZW50Z2jmq

Digital asset market structure has been years in the making, and the finish line is finally in sight. But the journey is far from over. Cato’s Ryan Chan-Wei examines what the CLARITY Act gets right, where it falls short, and what should come next.
ow.ly/iypl50Z2WHe

President Trump just turned a lawsuit he controlled—against himself—into a $1.8 billion slush fund with no congressional approval, no independent oversight, and no appeals. The 'Anti-Weaponization Fund' is more weaponization, explain Cato’s @DeHavenTad and Molly Nixon.   
ow.ly/nCxe50Z2Wv5

Cost-conscious Americans, beware:

If the Iran war drags on and escalates, the fiscal and financial costs will grow too, with downstream effects on Americans’ budgets, explains Cato’s @LettDominik.
ow.ly/9XW850Z2s37

The SEC spent 50 years silencing the people best positioned to expose its enforcement abuses. It just dropped that policy—not out of principle, but because speech-suppressing policy was at serious risk of being taken up by the Supreme Court. Cato has the receipts. ow.ly/5BGF50Z2Wpv

In light of rising inflation, the Federal Reserve should address affordability concerns by abandoning discretionary policymaking and returning to a data-driven, objective approach to setting interest rates, says Cato’s @JaiKedia.

ow.ly/lv1m50Z2nAf

The US indictment of Raúl Castro raises hope for an end to the Castro tyranny, says Cato’s @VasquezIan.

“When the Cuban dictatorship finally collapses, it would be best to let Cubans themselves determine their return to freedom.”

Video

Critical Race Theory being taught as fact in the classroom was and still is a real problem. But new state anti-DEI laws could dictate how these ideas are taught, even if they're introduced as theory. That’s not a fix—it's the same problem masquerading as reform, says Cato’s @Rhetors_of_York.

Video

As cryptocurrencies grow in popularity, they have become increasingly easy to use for everyday transactions. However, the US tax code has not kept pace. 

During a Capitol Hill briefing, Cato scholars @EconWithNick and @adamnmichel, along with Coin Center's @jasonsomensatto, discussed practical reforms to simplify the tax code, reduce compliance burdens, and expand Americans’ ability to choose how they transact.

Congress is slated to consider a $1.5 trillion defense budget that includes billions in new funding for munitions. But what caused the munitions shortage? 

Cato’s @katherinet57 argues America’s munitions arsenal has been drained significantly to arm Ukraine and prosecute the ongoing war in Iran without considering the long-term strategic costs. 

The defense budget should include reforms to protect US stockpiles from previous mistakes.  

ow.ly/y9oY50Z2rQT

Colorado Gov. Polis's commutation of Tina Peters's sentence was a dangerous decision. Presidents shouldn't secure state-level pardons of political allies by conditioning federal funds on the offender's release, and governors shouldn't accede to presidential extortion.

ow.ly/VZFR50Z2qIh

During a recent Cato Institute event, Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright praised the work of Cato's Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies @ts_fisher. 

Watch the full discussion on how America can unleash the next energy revolution: 
piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Video

Prosecutors hold a monopoly on criminal charges, often sidelining victims while enjoying immunity from suit. Cato’s Matthew Cavedon argues that private prosecutions would introduce choice and accountability for victims without expanding state coercion. 

ow.ly/r4Pp50Z2fgF

The Framers expected future presidents to use the pardon power judiciously. But blanket pardons for administration officials could effectively void the criminal laws that govern them, turning accountability into leverage and undermining the rule of law itself, explains Cato’s Molly Nixon.

ow.ly/3OLY50Z2cOz

Trump's new $1.8 billion "Anti-Weaponization Fund" lets a hand-picked committee pay political allies—bypassing Congress, judges, and any check on cronyism. That’s not redress; that’s just the weaponization of federal spending to benefit the president’s friends, explains Cato’s Dan Greenberg. 
ow.ly/9XgQ50Z2IOC

Many Americans think they understand today’s Supreme Court. But @whignewtons is here to tell you that’s wrong. Join us for a conversation with Sarah Isgur about what may be the last constitutionally functioning branch of American government. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1AKEmOEbw…

Two billion people use wood for heating and cooking instead of gas, causing millions of deaths. Energy Secretary @SecretaryWright hopes for the day when affordable propane and clean cookstoves are available to the world's poorest households.

Watch the full discussion on how America can unleash the next energy revolution: 
ow.ly/uBuY50Z1906

Video

“It’s time for Americans to know that the Bank Secrecy Act is really the Bank Surveillance Act—and it is time for Congress to fix it,” testified Cato’s @EconWithNick before a subcommittee of the House Committee on Financial Services. 

Watch his testimony here: ow.ly/Lyf550Z2JYn

The UAE's OPEC exit isn't about oil production—quotas were largely ignored anyway. OPEC functions more as a political club than a true cartel, and the UAE's departure signals shifting Gulf politics, not a market shakeup, explains Cato’s Peter Van Doren.

ow.ly/R6fP50Z1NQt
